ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The central skeleton in the figure is a sulfonyl chloride structure, the sulfur atom is connected to two oxygens by double bonds, and is connected to chlorine; the sulfur is also connected to the nitrogen on the left. The nitrogen on the left is connected to a methoxycarbonyl CH3O2C, and bears an N-H. There are two :NEt3 in the figure, the triethylamine arrow at the lower left points to the N-H proton, the triethylamine arrow on the right points to sulfur, while the electron arrow of the S-Cl bond points to chlorine. Reasoning: The left arrow indicates that triethylamine removes the N-H proton, and the N-H bond electrons remain on nitrogen, therefore this sulfonamide/carbamate nitrogen becomes negatively charged [N-], still connected to C(OC)=O and S(=O)2. The right arrow indicates that the lone pair electrons of triethylamine attack sulfur, and the S-Cl bond breaks to give chlorine; after triethylamine forms a bond with sulfur, nitrogen has four bonds, therefore it is [N+](CC)(CC)CC. Retaining the two S=O, the combination gives the product SMILES as O=S([N-]C(OC)=O)([N+](CC)(CC)CC)=O.

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First identify the starting skeleton in the image as CH3O2C-NH-S(=O)2-Cl. Follow the left arrow set: triethylamine removes the N-H proton, and the N-H bond electron pair remains on the sulfonamide/carbamate nitrogen, so that nitrogen becomes [N-] while still attached to C(OC)=O and S(=O)2. Follow the right arrow set: the lone pair of the right NEt3 attacks sulfur and the S-Cl bond breaks to chloride, replacing Cl by N(Et)3; because triethylamine now has four bonds, it is [N+](CC)(CC)CC. Combine the unchanged two S=O bonds, the anionic N-carbomethoxy substituent, and the cationic triethylammonium substituent on sulfur to write O=S([N-]C(OC)=O)([N+](CC)(CC)CC)=O.
